body.en: For "give the meaning as used in the passage", give a word or short phrase of the same part of speech that fits the sentence. For "why" and "how" questions, give the reason from the passage in your own words, not a copied sentence. For inference, state what is implied and point to the clue. For the summary, follow the instructions exactly (which part of the passage, points or prose, word limit), and leave out examples.

title.en: On the board: fill in with the correct form of the verb

say.en: Look at the time markers and the subject.

text.en: fill in with the correct form of the verb
By the time we (reach) the station, the train (leave).
By the time we reached the station, the train had left.
If I (know) the answer, I would have told you.
If I had known the answer, I would have told you.
The list of items (be) on the table.
The list of items is on the table.
She has lived (has been living) here since 2019.

passage.en: Scarcely had the match begun __1__ it started to rain. The committee __2__ already taken its decision when I arrived. He is interested __3__ astronomy, and he prefers stargazing __4__ watching television. If she __5__ harder, she would have passed.

explanation.en: Scarcely … when; past perfect for the earlier past action; interested in; prefer … to; third conditional uses had + past participle.

body.en: Common slips: giving a noun as the meaning of an adjective; copying a whole sentence as an answer; ignoring "in your own words"; writing "than" after scarcely or hardly; "despite of"; future tense after "when" or "if" in a time or condition clause; "prefer than"; missing articles; wrong verb agreement with each, every, one of. Read the instruction and the whole sentence before answering.

points.en: No will after if/when in time clauses

narration.en: Common slips: giving a noun as the meaning of an adjective; copying a whole sentence as an answer; ignoring "in your own words"; writing "than" after scarcely or hardly; "despite of"; future tense after "when" or "if" in a time or condition clause; "prefer than"; missing articles; wrong verb agreement with each, every, one of. text.en: Hardly had I reached home when the phone rang.
Hardly had I reached home than the phone rang.
Despite of the rain, the match continued.
I will call you when I reach Delhi.
I will call you when I will reach Delhi.
One of my friends lives in Pune.

explanation.en: hardly … when; despite without "of"; no will in the when-clause; one of + plural noun + singular verb.

problem.en: Passage clue: "Unlike his boisterous classmates, Arun sat quietly, his eyes fixed on the window." Give the meaning of "boisterous" and say what the writer suggests about Arun.

steps.en: "Unlike" shows a contrast with Arun, who is quiet.
So boisterous means noisy and lively (an adjective, like the word it replaces).
Arun is quiet and withdrawn; the fixed gaze at the window suggests he is lost in thought or unhappy.

answer.en: Boisterous: noisy and energetic. Arun seems withdrawn and preoccupied.
